endorsements.quote: Firstly, develop training and education resources to help clinicians understand and manage the ethical risks posed by AI.

These mechanisms should also be implemented at the organisational level, and may include embedding the reporting of AI tools to existing safety and quality improvement committees and ensuring procurement processes are redesigned to enable robust evaluation of the AI technology.

This includes integration of guidelines such as Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-Artificial Intelligence (CONSORT-AI) and Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials-Artificial Intelligence (SPIRIT-AI) as a standard and setting expectations for AI trial reporting and operations.

unlisted_practices: Develop a national strategy for ICUs to guide the ethical implementation of AI, aligned with existing National AI Frameworks.
Provide ethical evaluation frameworks and guidelines for AI in ICU, contextualising existing resources such as the National AI Ethics Principles.
Develop an ethical framework tailored to ICU leadership for AI procurement, implementation, and oversight.
Establish a diverse working group including patients, ethicists, and the wider ICU healthcare team to drive stakeholder engagement on ICU AI.
Include AI and ethics learning in professional regulatory requirements and accredit it for Continuing Professional Development.
Keep AI code open-source to promote openness and research scrutiny.
Keep clinicians actively involved in interpreting AI outputs through the lens of patient values and clinical context (human-in-the-loop).

screen.reason: This is an ethical commentary and framework paper providing recommendations for how ICU clinicians and health care systems should safely and ethically implement AI.
